build.reason: The supplied recipe defines the required encoding macro and links the parser library; the old setter remains declared with the harness's call signature. This is a static compatibility assessment, not an observed build.

input.reason: The entry passes the supplied bytes and an int-sized length to XML_Parse; its size assertion enforces the parser API's length range.

lifecycle.reason: The root remains alive while child parsers are created and parsed; the entry frees children before the root. Reset occurs after the helper's parsing calls.

control_flow.reason: The entry reaches root parsing, namespace parsing, and both child-creation calls. The full-salt configuration failure is assessed in the change groups.

accepted.requirement: Parser hashing on the target's parse and external-entity surface must be able to use a full 16-byte salt from a supported high-quality source, through XML_SetHashSalt16Bytes before parsing or Expat's automatic generation.
accepted.target_route: LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput creates root and namespace parsers, then calls ParseOneInput, which derives an unsigned-long SipHash value from the input, calls XML_SetHashSalt, and calls XML_Parse. It later creates, parses, and frees two child parsers.
accepted.failure_condition: For a finite valid XML input whose derived salt is nonzero, XML_SetHashSalt sets the upper key word to zero, writes only the unsigned-long value to the lower word, and sets the salt flag. XML_Parse therefore skips automatic full-salt generation, and internal hashing uses the limited key.
accepted.alternative_paths: The namespace parser uses the same helper. Children inherit the parent's salt and flag and also use that helper. No parser route calls XML_SetHashSalt16Bytes. A zero derived salt can leave automatic generation available, but it does not satisfy the full-salt requirement for the nonzero-salt condition assessed here.

source_evidence.quote:
#47 #1183  CVE-2026-41080 -- The existing hash flooding protection
                    (based on SipHash) only used 4 to 8 bytes of entropy for
                    a salt, when 16 bytes of salt are supported by the
                    implementation of SipHash used by Expat. Now full 16 bytes
                    of entropy are used to improve protection against hash
                    flooding attacks.
                      Existing API function XML_SetHashSalt is now deprecated
                    because of its limitations, and its use should be
                    considered a vulnerability. Please either use the new API
                    function XML_SetHashSalt16Bytes (with known-high-quality
                    entropy input only!) instead, or leave the derivation of
                    a 16-bytes hash salt from high quality entropy to Expat's
                    internal machinery (by *not* calling either of the two
                    XML_SetHashSalt* functions).

Sets the hash salt to use for internal hash calculations. Helps in preventing DoS attacks based on predicting hash function behavior. In order to have an effect this must be called before parsing has started. Returns XML_TRUE if successful, XML_FALSE when called after XML_Parse or XML_ParseBuffer or when parser is NULL.

Note: Setting a salt that is not from a source of high quality entropy (like getentropy(3)) will make the parser vulnerable to hash flooding attacks.

Note: This call is optional, as the parser will auto-generate a new random salt value internally if no value has been set by the start of parsing.
